narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed by our credit assessment system, which evaluated your financial profile and determined a predicted likelihood of bad credit risk at 51% — just above the threshold required for approval. While this is a borderline result, it was enough to result in a denial, and understanding the specific factors behind this decision may help you take steps to strengthen a future application.

The single most influential factor working against your application was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, nearly half had no checking account at all, and the majority of the rest maintained positive balances. A negative checking account balance is a strong signal of financial strain, and it weighed most heavily in the model's assessment of your situation.

The second most important factor was your credit history. Your record shows no prior credits or all credits fully paid — which might sound positive, but in practice it means there is very little evidence of how you manage ongoing debt obligations over time. In contrast, the vast majority of approved applicants had a history of existing credits that were being actively and successfully repaid, or even some past difficulties that were resolved. Lenders and credit models tend to view a demonstrated track record of managing credit more favorably than a near-blank slate, because it provides concrete evidence of repayment behavior.

On a more positive note, your property ownership — specifically your real estate — actually worked in your favor and pushed the assessment toward a more favorable outcome. Owning real estate is seen as a sign of financial stability and provides a form of security, and this factor partially offset the concerns raised by the other two.

There are also a few contextual details worth noting: you are requesting a relatively modest amount of 1,108 DM for home repairs over just 12 months, both of which are well below the averages seen among approved applicants. However, your installment rate — the share of your disposable income going toward repayments — is set at 4%, which is higher than the average of about 2.94% among approved applicants, meaning the repayments would represent a comparatively larger burden on your budget. You also already have two existing credits at this bank, compared to an average of about 1.4 among approved applicants, which adds to the picture of financial pressure.

As a next step, we strongly encourage you to work on bringing your checking account into a positive balance before reapplying, as this was the most decisive factor in the denial. Building a clearer credit history — for example, by successfully managing a smaller credit product — could also significantly improve your profile. Speaking with a financial advisor or a bank representative about your specific situation may help you identify the fastest path toward a successful application in the future.
